claim: Barcelona Sants to Girona high-speed trains run ~30/day, fastest ~38 min, average ~1 hour, on AVE/Avant/Euromed, with fares from roughly $9 when booked in advance.
quote: The route's fastest journey takes 38 minutes... There are around 30 trains per day... Train tickets from Barcelona to Girona start from as little as $8.92... You can travel from Barcelona to Girona on AVE, Renfe, Avant and Euromed trains.

claim: Girona's Temps de Flors 2026 runs May 9-17, daily 9:30am-9pm, free admission, with floral installations in monuments, courtyards and gardens across the old town.
quote: FROM MAY 9 TO 17 2026... Every day from 9.30 am. to 9 pm... Free... Embellishment and floral art installations in monuments, courtyards and gardens around the city.

claim: Girona-Costa Brava airport (GRO) sits ~18km from the city; bus 607 runs hourly to the centre in ~20-25 min, and a Barcelona Bus links the airport to Barcelona Estacio del Nord in ~1h10.
quote: Bus number 607 running hourly between 4:00am and midnight... travel from the city center to the airport in 20 to 25 minutes... the Barcelona Bus service leaves Girona airport for Barcelona Estació del Nord with a journey time of 1 hour and 10 minutes.

claim: Two to three days is ideal for a Girona weekend; the compact historic core can be toured in 4-5 hours, and a third day suits day trips to Figueres or Besalu.
quote: A weekend (two to three days) in Girona will provide you with more time... you can easily tour the city... in as little as 4 or 5 hours... If you have three days, spend your final day on a day trip... Figueres and Besalú are great options.

claim: Girona is small and walkable; it is best not to bring a car into town, and everything is reachable on foot with 10 local bus routes as backup.
quote: Girona is a walkable city and easy to explore on foot... it's best not to bring a car into town... The town is small enough that you can likely walk anywhere you want to go, but if you need transit, there are 10 local bus routes.

claim: Barri Vell (Old Town) is the best base for first-timers, putting the Cathedral and Jewish Quarter within walking distance, with Eixample across the river as a cheaper alternative and Mercadal good for families.
quote: staying in Barri Vell makes the most sense as it puts you right in the middle of the main sights... Eixample is a great option and it's just across the river from the old town... Mercadal is a great option where you're within easy reach of the main sights.

claim: Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) are the best times to visit Girona, around 20-22C, while July-August regularly hit 30-33C with peak crowds.
quote: Spring (April-May) and Autumn (September-October) are widely recommended as the ideal periods... temperatures in July and August regularly reach 30-33°C... The best times to visit Girona are from mid-May to mid-June and from mid-September to mid-October.
